newsitem.title: CANADA: Pacalta to drill up to 20 Ecuador wells - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Pacalta to drill up to 20 Ecuador wells - CEO.

text.p: Pacalta Resources Ltd president and chief executive John Wright said on Monday that the company would drill up to 20 wells on its recently acquired Ecuardor properties in the next 15 months.
"(That's a) total capital expenditure of pretty close to US$42 million," Wright told Reuters after a presentation at a FirstEnergy Capital Corp energy conference.
He said the capital expenditures would be funded through working capital, future cash flow and a bank line the company was working to establish.
"We are just in the final stages of negotiating that now," Wright added.
The wells would be drilled in Ecuador's City Block, which already has 18 producing wells, and on the fivefold-larger Block 27.
Wright said he could not forecast the new wells' impact on production because the company was in registration for its most recent security issue.
He said FirstEnergy Capital Corp analyst Martin Molyneaux had forecast Ecuadorian production would surge to 15,000 barrels a day next year from about 5,500 barrels currently.

"And that's absolutely within the realm of possibility. If you think about it...we're going to drill up to 20 wells and each of those wells, even if it's average, will give us up to 1,000 barrels per day. But obviously some of those will be dry," Wright said.
Pacalta acquired its Ecuador properties this year through two transactions that gave it 100 percent of City Investing Co of Bermuda.
The Ecuador acquisition catapulted it to the international oil and gas scene and substantially increased its reserves.
Wright said operations in the Ecuador fields kept Pacalta occupied for the moment.
"At the moment, we have our plate full. But opportunities are being presented to us regularly, so I can't say we're not planning that. We have nothing in our crosshairs at the moment," he said.
But Pacalta is looking for strategic alliances in Latin America with service companies and pipeline companies.
The first type of alliance would allow it to cement its relationship with service providers with incentive plans.

The second sort of pact will allow it to lock in its pipeline capacity. But Pacalta has no plans to give up a stake in its projects. Wright said Pacalta was examining the possibility of setting up a barge-based export program into the Brazilian market, or a topping plant or a power generation project or combination of all three.
Pacalta shares were 0.35 higher at 8.70 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday.
"The market has given us a lot of confidence. We have got a lot of pressure to perform. We're not sitting back, that's for sure," Wright said.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
